keyframes.prompt: Vertical 2:3 underwater nature photo of a shallow freshwater pond, side view, camera under the water looking straight ahead. The top of the frame shows the calm water surface seen from below, with floating green aquatic plants on the left and right, and one clear open circle in the plants in the center. Just under the surface in that open circle floats one flat patch of hundreds of tiny round amber-yellow fish eggs, about half of the frame width wide; each egg is very small, about one eightieth of the frame width. Below: slightly green clear water, a few thin plant stems, and a muddy bottom with dead leaves at the very bottom of the frame. Soft sunlight rays from above. Keep everything important away from the left and right edges. No fish. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the water surface, the floating plants, the open circle, the stems, the muddy bottom, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The eggs are hatching: hundreds of tiny newly hatched fish larvae hang just under the surface in the same patch. Each larva is a thin transparent sliver with a round yellow yolk sac and two dark eyes, about one fortieth of the frame width long. Some empty egg shells remain. No adult fish. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the water surface, the floating plants, the open circle, the stems, the muddy bottom, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The larvae and egg shells are gone. In the same place, just under the surface, a dense school of hundreds of small deep orange fish fry swims close together in one round ball, about half of the frame width wide. Each fry is bright orange with dark eyes, about one twenty-fifth of the frame width long. No adult fish. No text, no watermark.

It is tan colored with dark brown stripes along its body, a thin orange stripe along its side, and one small dark eye spot on the rear end of its long dorsal fin, about one quarter of the frame width long. Only one fish. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the water surface, the floating plants, the open circle, the stems, the muddy bottom, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The young fish is now an adult striped snakehead in the same place and pose, head facing left: long round body, large flat snake-like head with big scales, wide mouth, long dorsal fin along the whole back, long anal fin, rounded tail fin. The back is dark black-brown, the sides are mottled black and ochre with faint dark bands, the belly is white. It is about three fifths of the frame width long, fully inside the frame. Only one fish. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the water surface, the floating plants, the open circle, the stems, the muddy bottom, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The same adult snakehead, with the same size and colors, stays in the same place and pose. Above it, just under the surface in the open circle, floats a new flat patch of hundreds of tiny round amber-yellow eggs. Only one fish. No text, no watermark.
